title: Sabre
one_paragraph_synopsis: In this episode, Dunder Mifflin adjusts to its new ownership by Sabre, an electronics company focused on selling printers. Michael and the office receive new equipment and face new policies introduced by Gabe Lewis, the coordinating director. Michael struggles with the changes, including environmental initiatives and restricted office resources, while seeking advice from Jo and visiting David Wallace, who shares a new business idea. Meanwhile, Jim and Pam navigate awkward social moments, and the office tries to welcome Gabe despite uncertainty about the future.

main_threads.thread: The transition of Dunder Mifflin to Sabre ownership and the introduction of new policies and equipment.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Oh! Wow. Awesome. For accounting, a brand new printer. And for the sales staff, a new fax machine.
Michael: It's from "Sob-ray", our new owner, and it is to Sabre, us.
Gabe: Um, hi, uh, my name is Gabe Lewis. I am coordinating director for merging regions.
Gabe: Most of our business comes from selling printers. So don't think of yourselves as paper salesmen anymore, but as printer salesmen who also sell paper.
Gabe: We have a policy here at Sabre where we are, uh, allowed to take two weeks.
Gabe: Ok, did everyone get one? With these bottles, we eliminate the need for plastic water bottles, which are the scourge of the environment.

main_threads.thread: Michael's mixed feelings and resistance to Sabre's changes, including environmental policies and office restrictions.

evidence.snippet: Michael: I don't want to appear ungrateful for everything Sabre's doing for us.

Jo: So listen, why don't you tell Gabe if by the end of the day you can't handle the changes.
